rows.evidence: Re-checked from scratch (changed). Both pages now carry (rendered by refs.js as a reference link, the same ungraded-pointer markup S7 L05 uses). Registry: DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1997.tb03807.x, 'The Limits of Arbitrage', Shleifer & Vishny, JF 52(1) 35-55, 1997. WebFetch 2026-10-23 of https://ms.mcmaster.ca/%7Egrasselli/ShleiferVishny97.pdf (JSTOR-stamped): p. 37 'performance based arbitrage' defined; p. 38 Section I 'An Agency Model of Limited Arbitrage' begins (noise traders, arbitrageurs, investors in arbitrage funds); pp. 39-40 funds F_t, investors allocate by past returns, eq. (4) G increasing in gross return; p. 41 eq. (5) G(x) = ax + 1 - a, a >= 1, 'if a > 1, funds are actually withdrawn in response to poor performance'; p. 45 Proposition 3 'If arbitrageurs are fully invested at t = 1, and noise trader [misperceptions deepen at t = 2] ... then, for a > 1, F2 < D1 and F2/p2 < D1/p1'; no proof given. So locator 'pp. 38-41; Proposition 3, p. 45' points at the model set-up and the result. L01 prose: 'a model ... in which specialized arbitrageurs invest other people's money and, when funds respond strongly enough to past performance, investors withdraw funds after poor performance' = pp. 38-41 with a > 1 in words (no symbol). L02 prose: 'a model of arbitrageurs who invest other people's money, in which such a trade may have to be cut back when the mispricing widens' = Proposition 3, modal and model-scoped. Numeric sanity check (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/6f74c4e7-484a-542c-982f-ae21506915ed/scratchpad/L01-L02-r4/py: SV fund equation F2 = F1 + aD1(p2/p1 - 1), V=1, F1=0.2, S1=0.3, S2=0.4, the paper's own example values as restated in Arnold DP 418 Example 2): a = 1.2 gives p1 0.9 -> p2 0.764, F2 0.164 < D1 0.2 and F2/p2 < D1/p1, i.e. positions are cut; Arnold's Example 2 confirms this full-investment equilibrium exists for q < 0.359. Attribution accurate.
